airport: Airports show long, straight runways with distinct markings, connected to large terminal buildings, hangars, and aircraft parking stands. They differ from viaducts by being ground-level aviation infrastructure rather than elevated road structures; farmland shows crop rows and field boundaries rather than aviation facilities; railway stations show train tracks and platforms rather than runways.
bareland: Bare land appears as exposed soil or rock surfaces with minimal vegetation, showing smooth to uneven textures and light brown tones. It contrasts with desert by lacking sand dune formations and being less uniformly sandy; farmland shows crop rows and organized field patterns; mountains show elevated rocky peaks with shadowed slopes.
baseballfield: Baseball fields show diamond-shaped infields with visible pitcher's mound, baselines, and outfield grass. They differ from parks by having sports diamond markings rather than natural wooded areas; stadiums by being open fields without large surrounding stands; ponds by being land-based sports facilities rather than water bodies.
beach: Beaches appear as sandy or pebbly shorelines along water bodies, with light colors and wave patterns. They contrast with desert by being coastal sandy areas adjacent to water rather than inland dunes; ports show docks, ships, and industrial infrastructure rather than natural sand; rivers show flowing water channels rather than shoreline deposits.
bridge: Bridges show elevated roadway or railway structures spanning over water or valleys, with visible pillars and deck. They differ from viaducts by spanning over water rather than land with multiple supports; rivers show water channels without bridge structures; ponds are small water bodies without any crossing infrastructure.
center: Centers are characterized by high-density commercial buildings, large plazas, and major public structures with dense street networks. They contrast with stadiums by having mixed-use towers and offices rather than sports arenas; churches show religious architecture with spires rather than commercial blocks; commercial areas have retail signage and parking rather than civic plazas.
church: Churches show distinctive religious architecture with prominent spires, steeples, or domes, often with a central nave and surrounding parking. They differ from centers by being smaller standalone religious buildings rather than dense commercial blocks; dense residential shows housing units without religious structures; schools show campus buildings and sports fields rather than spires.
commercial: Commercial areas show dense retail and office buildings with large parking lots, wide streets, and visible storefronts. They contrast with centers by having more retail-oriented structures rather than civic public buildings; squares show paved public plazas without retail blocks; stadiums show large sports venues rather than commercial buildings.
denseresidential: Dense residential features tightly packed housing units with small yards, narrow streets, and uniform block patterns. It differs from medium residential by having smaller lot sizes and less green space; sparse residential shows wider spacing and more vegetation; churches show single religious buildings rather than housing blocks.
desert: Deserts show vast, barren landscapes with sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse dry vegetation. They contrast with beaches by being inland sandy areas without water adjacency; bare land lacks dune formations and is less uniform; rivers show water channels rather than sandy terrain.
farmland: Farmland appears as large, open agricultural fields with uniform crop rows, regular field boundaries, and occasional irrigation. It differs from meadow by having organized crop rows rather than natural grassland; industrial areas show factories and storage rather than crops; bare land shows exposed soil without any crop patterns.
forest: Forests show dense tree canopy with dark green textures, irregular edges, and no visible ground. They contrast with ponds by having dense vegetation rather than water features; desert by having dense tree cover rather than sand; bare land shows exposed soil without any tree canopy.
industrial: Industrial areas feature large warehouses, factories, smokestacks, and extensive parking lots with regular blocky layouts. They differ from storage tanks by having buildings and smokestacks rather than circular metallic containers; farmland shows agricultural fields rather than factories; railway stations show tracks and passenger buildings rather than industrial structures.
meadow: Meadows show open, grassy areas with smooth, uniform texture, often with scattered trees, and no field lines. They contrast with farmland by lacking organized crop rows and field boundaries; bare land shows exposed soil without grass cover; baseball fields have sports markings and infield dirt rather than natural grass.
mediumresidential: Medium residential shows moderately sized houses on medium lots with visible yards, driveways, and tree-lined streets. It differs from dense residential by having larger lots and more green space; sparse residential shows widely spaced houses with large wooded lots; resorts show hotel buildings, pools, and recreational facilities rather than residential neighborhoods.
mountain: Mountains show elevated, rugged terrain with steep slopes, rocky outcrops, and shadow patterns. They contrast with bare land by having dramatic elevation and rock formations rather than flat exposed soil; deserts show sand dunes rather than rocky peaks; forests show tree cover without exposed rock.
park: Parks show green open spaces with trees, walking paths, ponds, and recreational areas, often irregular in shape. They differ from squares by being paved public plazas without extensive grass; baseball fields are sports-specific with diamond markings; ponds are smaller water features within park landscapes.
parking: Parking lots appear as flat, paved areas with rows of vehicles, clear lane markings, and entrance points. They differ from airports by having no runways or aircraft and being smaller in scale; dense residential shows housing units rather than vehicle storage; ports show water, docks, and ships rather than parked vehicles.
playground: Playgrounds show recreational areas with equipment like slides, swings, and courts, often within parks or schools. They differ from stadiums by being smaller recreational zones without large stands; parks are larger green areas with paths and trees; meadows show open grass without recreational structures.
pond: Ponds appear as small, circular or irregular water bodies with calm surfaces, often surrounded by vegetation. They contrast with rivers by being still, enclosed water rather than flowing channels; parks are larger green areas with paths and trees rather than just water; farmland shows crop fields rather than water features.
port: Ports show waterfront areas with docks, piers, ships, cranes, and large storage areas adjacent to water. They differ from resorts by having industrial waterfront infrastructure rather than hotels and pools; beaches show natural sandy shorelines without port facilities; storage tanks show metallic containers inland rather than docks and ships.
railwaystation: Railway stations show tracks, platforms, passenger buildings, and surrounding parking lots, often with linear rail lines. They contrast with industrial areas by having passenger buildings and platforms rather than factories; viaducts show elevated rail structures rather than ground-level stations; airports have runways and terminals rather than train tracks.
resort: Resorts show hotel buildings, pools, tennis courts, and landscaped grounds, often near beaches. They differ from ports by having recreational facilities and hotels rather than docks and ships; parks have natural vegetation and paths rather than hotel buildings; beaches show natural sand without built resort infrastructure.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, sinuous, dark water channels with flowing patterns and riparian vegetation. They contrast with ponds by being elongated flowing water rather than still enclosed water bodies; bridges are structures spanning across rivers; beaches show sandy shorelines along water rather than the water channels themselves.
school: Schools show campus layouts with classroom buildings, playgrounds, sports fields, and surrounding parking lots. They differ from squares by having educational facilities rather than public plazas; churches show religious architecture rather than school buildings; parks show natural vegetation and paths rather than campus facilities.
sparseresidential: Sparse residential shows widely separated houses surrounded by large vegetated lots, with unpaved roads and low building density. It contrasts with medium residential by having larger lot sizes and more vegetation; forests show tree cover without housing; ponds are small water features within residential areas.
square: Squares show paved public plazas with geometric layouts, central monuments or fountains, and surrounding buildings. They differ from parks by being paved with minimal grass and formal geometry; commercial areas have retail buildings rather than open plazas; schools have campus buildings rather than public gathering spaces.
stadium: Stadiums show large sports or event venues with oval or rectangular shape, tiered seating, and surrounding parking. They contrast with playgrounds by having enclosed stands and much larger scale; centers show commercial towers rather than sports venues; baseball fields are open fields without surrounding stadium structures.
storagetanks: Storage tanks appear as large circular metallic containers with domed or flat roofs, arranged in industrial clusters. They differ from industrial areas by being rows of tanks rather than factories and smokestacks; ports show waterfront docks rather than tank farms; farmland shows agricultural fields rather than metallic containers.
viaduct: Viaducts show elevated road or rail structures with long continuous sections and multiple supports, often crossing over land. They differ from bridges by spanning over land rather than water; railway stations are ground-level with tracks rather than elevated structures; airports show ground-level aviation facilities rather than elevated roads.
